newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse says CBS results to improve.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse says CBS results to improve.

text.p: The chairman of Westinghouse Electric Corp said Wednesday results at its CBS television network should be boosted in the coming months by improved ratings and the broadcast of the '98 winter Olympic games.

"We've gained share in the key demographic groups in the '96-'97 season and we expect to continue to gain share against our rivals, and that will help our results," Michael Jordan, Westinghouse chairman, said at a press briefing immediately following the company's annual meeting in Minneapolis.
Jordan also said results at the network should be buoyed next year when it broadcasts the '98 winter Olympics in February.
Earnings at the CBS television network fell in the first quarter. Westinghouse blamed the decline on lower demographic ratings among younger viewers.

Jordan said he expects Westinghouse's stock price to rise during the next several weeks as television ratings improve. He said the stock should be trading in a range of $18 to $19 per share by the time Westinghouse separates its media and industrial businesses, scheduled to be completed by the end of the third quarter.
Shares were down 1/8 to 16-7/8 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Jordan declined to comment on earnings projections for the second quarter. Wall Street's consensus estimate for the quarter is a loss of $0.01 per share versus a profit of $0.06 last year, according to First Call.
